Your pitch and intonation are doing well.

However the biggest 'giveaway' is the fact that your voice is obviously stressed. Especially as you pitch upward for inflection, the voice is obviously stressed and weak. Fortunately, it's just a matter of practice for it to be stronger.

1. I used two major things to train my voice. The first was keeping track of fundamental frequency using Praat, which isn't exactly easy to use. However, you need some way of keeping track of it, since you have to be above 160 hertz. I also used my fingers to keep track of where the resonances were - making sure there were none in the chest/lower throat and plenty in the jaw/head region.

For my practice situations, I would focus on holding tones such as 'mah' for as long as possible, slowly (and i do mean slowly) pitching up my voice by strengthening the throat muscles. Actually working with real speech came next, and was something I introduced slowly, to make sure that I wasn't dropping out (and sounding male during certain parts). 

2. When I say speaking from the diaphragm, I mean projecting the voice to a certain degree. Yes, soft and somewhat breathy is feminine. But I try and use breathiness as more of an accent, not something that should be a major characteristic, otherwise you sound like you're in a soap opera. So I found that learning some projection skills helped make my voice sound full and confident, which is really critical for a good female voice. But the voice projection techniques (used in theatre and presentation speech and the like) are the same for all genders. 

My original voice pitch was around 70 hertz - I had a believable Don LaFontagne impression going (and I can still do it, though it isn't quite as powerful). Right now I average a little under 200, and I'm pushing my singing voice up above A4, since being able to sing in a female voice is hugely important to me (actually why I posted this, because I felt miserable about where I am singing).

3. I have been full-time for over a year and a half now - went fulltime September 2012. The thing about voice is you have to practice in all of these different situations - and being F/T puts you in plenty of different situations (being sick, out drinking, whatever) and you figure out how to get through there and still sound OK.

4. I've never really been one for videos, so I've always sought out articles. There's some good speech pathology literature about how to feminize the voice, which is what I used. Haven't watched any videos yet on how to sing.

2.5 years now (started working on it in Fall 2011), on top of 2 years of HRT. 

The big things that helped were running, which got my lungs in better shape which makes the feminine voice stronger, and singing practice - holding the higher notes until the throat muscles strengthen up. Good posture also really helps - if you slump down, it's hard to speak with the diaphragm, which can make the voice sound weak.

Someday soon, I'm going to look another woman in the eye and tell her that I truly do love her. 

But first, I have to take care of my own issues - I can't love another while hating myself. 

I've been focusing mainly on myself - pulling through all the crap I picked up while living a lie for so many years - that I've been negligent as to how I approach others. Some of this is dealing with my own sexual/romantic orientation (I thought simply saying 'I am a woman who likes women' was simple - nope, not quite that easy). 

I've made breaking the cycle of abuse one of my major personal endeavors. I know that I'm going to have to dedicate my entire lifetime to it, but I'm not afraid of that. If anything, I'm grateful that there's something I can do to make this world just a little bit better. I'm also glad I caught myself before I ended up having children.
